# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** [Associate]
**Date:** November 20, 2026
**Re:** Prodeth Water Solutions, Inc. / Toulous Aquachem LLC: review of the transaction folder (APA dated September 14, 2026) and issues for Prodeth before Closing
**Privileged & Confidential: Attorney Work Product**

---

## 1. Summary

I reviewed all nine documents in the folder:

1. Asset Purchase Agreement (APA)
2. Fannick Executive Employment Agreement
3. Bill of Sale and Assignment and Assumption Agreement
4. Subordinated Promissory Note (Seller Note)
5. Indemnity Escrow Agreement
6. Toulous Board Consent
7. Closing Side Letter
8. Joint Press Release
9. Mutual Confidentiality Agreement

**Deal terms**

- Purchase Price is **$42,000,000** (APA §2.5). It is paid as:
  - cash at Closing, of which **$3,150,000** goes into indemnity escrow with Pellucid Bank & Trust, N.A.; and
  - a **$6,000,000 Seller Note**. The Note is subordinated, carries 6% interest and matures 36 months after Closing.
- The APA is governed by **New York** law (§11.9). Its exclusive forum is the **State or federal courts in New York County** (§11.10).
- Seller's general indemnity cap (the **Cap Amount**) is **$4,200,000** (§9.5(a)).
- Closing has not occurred. The Outside Date is **January 15, 2027** (§10.1(b)).

**Six issues need to be fixed before Closing.** Most of them only appear when two documents, or two sections, are read together. In order of priority:

| # | Issue | Principal location | Exposure |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Side letter narrows the environmental carve-out from the cap | Side Letter §2 / APA §9.5(b)(iii) | Unknown contamination becomes subject to the $4.2M cap |
| 2 | Buyer's indemnity for Assumed Liabilities is uncapped and covers Seller's pre-Closing contract breaches | APA §§2.3(c), 9.3(b), 9.5(d) | Unlimited |
| 3 | Ashcombe consent is not a Required Consent or a closing condition | APA §§4.5(a), 7.2(c); Board Consent §1.5, Res. 3 | Closing without the contract behind ~31% of revenue |
| 4 | Seller Note uses Delaware law and forum; set-off sits under New York law and forum | Note §12; APA §§9.8, 11.9–11.12 | Split litigation; Note enforced without set-off |
| 5 | 9-month survival ends before the 12-month NSF recertification audit | APA §§9.1(a), 6.10, 4.14 | NSF representation claim expires unused |
| 6 | Seller Note is freely transferable, including to competitors | Note §10.1 (with §7) | Competitor receives Prodeth's financials and customer data |

---

## 2. Issues

### Issue 1: The Closing Side Letter shrinks the environmental carve-out from the cap

**Where:** Closing Side Letter §2, together with APA §1.1 ("Pre-Closing Environmental Liabilities"), §9.5(a)–(b)(iii) and §11.12.

**What the documents say**

- **The APA as signed.** "Pre-Closing Environmental Liabilities" covers all Liabilities under Environmental Laws from any Release or environmental condition at or migrating from any Purchased Asset, including the Ashby Falls Facility, existing on or before Closing. It applies "whether known or unknown and whether or not disclosed in the Disclosure Schedule or in any environmental report."
- **How the cap works.** §9.5(a) caps Seller's liability under §9.2(a) and §9.2(c) at the **$4,200,000 Cap Amount**. §9.5(b)(iii) then says the cap "shall not apply to Losses constituting Pre-Closing Environmental Liabilities, whether claimed under Section 9.2(a) or Section 9.2(c)." That is a strong buyer protection.
- **What the side letter does.** It is presented as a remediation undertaking. However:
  - it is expressly entered into under APA §11.8, and §5.1 confirms it is an amendment; and
  - §2 states that the definition "is hereby amended and restated in its entirety." The new definition covers only Liabilities arising from the **"Identified Environmental Conditions."** Those are the five recognized environmental conditions from the Kestrel Ridge Phase I Report, listed in **Annex A**.
- **Why it wins.** Under APA §11.12, an amendment entered into under §11.8 ranks *first* in the order of precedence, ahead of the APA itself.

**Why it matters to Prodeth**

- The carve-out from the cap would be limited to the five Annex A conditions:
  - the former UST;
  - the alum/PACl tank farm;
  - the historic drum area;
  - Outfall 001; and
  - the rail spur.
- Undiscovered contamination falls outside the carve-out. Examples include subsurface releases elsewhere at the site, PFAS, acrylamide or epichlorohydrin in groundwater not identified in a Phase I, and off-site migration.
- Those unidentified conditions would also cease to be Excluded Liabilities under APA §2.4(a). Because Excluded Liabilities are defined by reference to the amended term, they would no longer be clearly retained by Seller.
- Prodeth's recovery would then depend on the §4.13 environmental representation. That representation is knowledge-qualified, survives only 9 months, is subject to the $210,000 basket, and is limited by the $4,200,000 cap.
- A Phase I is by design a non-intrusive assessment. Unknown subsurface conditions are exactly the risk the original carve-out was drafted to cover.
- The remediation covenant in side letter §3 is useful, but it does not offset this loss of protection. It is also only an efforts obligation as to timing (24 months, commercially reasonable efforts).

**Recommended fix**

- **Preferred:** delete side letter §2 entirely. Keep the remediation undertaking as a standalone Seller covenant (as §5.2 already does) using a separate defined term for the Annex A work.
- **Fallback:** add language stating that the restated definition applies only for purposes of side letter §3. For purposes of APA §§2.4(a), 9.2(c) and 9.5(b)(iii), the original APA definition continues to apply, covering all pre-Closing conditions, known or unknown.
- **In either case:**
  - confirm that the remediation covenant is uncapped. A §9.2(b) covenant claim is already outside the §9.5(a) cap, but this should be stated expressly;
  - make completion of the Remedial Work (and obtaining a no-further-action letter) a hard obligation; and
  - consider a specific escrow or holdback for it.

---

### Issue 2: Uncapped Buyer indemnity for Assumed Liabilities, which include Seller's pre-Closing contract liabilities

**Where:** APA §2.3(c), §9.3(b), §9.5(c)–(d) and §9.1(c).

**What the documents say**

- §2.3(c) makes Buyer assume "all Liabilities under the Assigned Contracts, **whether arising before or after the Closing**."
- §9.3(b) requires Buyer to indemnify Seller for any Assumed Liability.
- §9.5(c) caps Buyer's indemnity at the Cap Amount. But §9.5(d) provides that "**no limitation in this Section 9.5** shall apply to Buyer's obligations under Section 9.3(b)."
- §9.1(c) lets claims under §9.3(b) be made at any time.

**Why it matters to Prodeth**

- Read together, Prodeth takes on, with no cap and no time limit, liability for Seller's own pre-Closing performance under the Ashcombe, Brennock, Tillery and other municipal supply contracts. That includes:
  - off-spec or non-NSF-conforming deliveries;
  - late-delivery penalties and liquidated damages;
  - price-adjustment true-ups and credits; and
  - potential third-party claims from utilities (for example, treatment failures).
- Prodeth must also indemnify Seller if a counterparty pursues Seller for these liabilities.
- This sits awkwardly with §2.4, under which Seller retains its pre-Closing liabilities generally. It also undercuts the §4.5(b) "no material breach" representation, which is itself capped and expires after 9 months.
- Pricing assumed only post-Closing performance. As drafted, Prodeth bears an open-ended tail on a business it did not run.

**Recommended fix**

- Amend §2.3(c) to read: "all Liabilities under the Assigned Contracts **to the extent arising out of performance required after the Closing**, excluding any Liability arising from any breach or default by Seller at or before the Closing."
- Add a matching item to §2.4: "all Liabilities under the Assigned Contracts arising from Seller's performance or breach at or before the Closing."
- Delete §9.5(d), or at minimum limit it to post-Closing Assumed Liabilities.
- Make clear that any pre-Closing contract liability is a Seller-retained, indemnifiable Excluded Liability.

---

### Issue 3: Ashcombe County Water Authority consent is not a Required Consent or a closing condition

**Where:** APA §2.1(c), §4.5(a), §6.3, §7.2(c) and §3.2(d); Toulous Board Consent §1.5 and Resolution 3.

**What the documents say**

- The Ashcombe Supply Agreement is an Assigned Contract (APA §2.1(c)).
- APA §4.5(a) defines the "**Required Consents**" as only the Brennock and Tillery consents, and represents that no other consent is needed.
- Buyer's condition in §7.2(c), Seller's efforts covenant in §6.3 and the deliverable in §3.2(d) are all tied to the Required Consents.
- Toulous's own board consent (September 10, 2026) recites two things:
  - the Ashcombe Supply Agreement was about **31% of the Business's 2025 revenue**; and
  - the agreement prohibits assignment, or any "sale of all or substantially all of the assets used in its performance," without the **prior written consent of the Authority**.
- Resolution 3 only authorizes officers to "*seek*" that consent. By contrast, for Brennock and Tillery the board directs officers to "seek and obtain" consent and deliver it to Prodeth.
- Nothing in the folder shows the Ashcombe consent has been requested or obtained.

**Why it matters to Prodeth**

- Under the APA as drafted, Ashcombe consent is **not** a condition to Prodeth's obligation to close. If the Authority refuses consent or terminates, Prodeth could still be required to close and pay the full $42,000,000 without the Business's largest customer contract.
- The §7.2(a) bring-down condition, which relies on §4.5(a) being accurate, and the §7.2(e) MAE condition are weak, contestable routes to avoid closing.
- After Closing, Prodeth's remedy is a breach claim under the §4.5(a) representation. That claim is subject to:
  - the $210,000 basket;
  - the $4,200,000 cap; and
  - the 9-month survival period.
- On the Seller's own board record, the §4.5(a) representation appears to be inaccurate.

**Recommended fix**

- Before Closing, amend APA §4.5(a) to add "(iii) the consent of the Ashcombe County Water Authority under the Ashcombe Supply Agreement" to the Required Consents. This automatically brings it within §§3.2(d), 6.3 and 7.2(c).
- Make sure the consent covers both assignment and the asset sale. It should also confirm that there is no default and no termination right arising from the Transaction.
- Alternatively, require the signed consent to be delivered as a precondition to Prodeth signing any closing documents.
- Also consider:
  - a specific indemnity, outside the cap, for losses if the Ashcombe contract is lost or terminated because of the Transaction;
  - a purchase price adjustment mechanism; and
  - extending the Outside Date if consent remains pending.
- Prodeth must give prior written consent (which may be by email) before Toulous shares Prodeth information with the Authority (Confidentiality Agreement §3.3). We should be ready to give that consent promptly.

---

### Issue 4: Seller Note governing law and forum (Delaware) conflict with the APA set-off regime (New York)

**Where:** Seller Note §12.1–12.2; APA §9.8, §11.9, §11.10 and §11.12.

**What the documents say**

- APA §9.8 gives Prodeth a right to set off indemnity amounts (both finally determined amounts and pending good-faith claims) against principal and interest on the Seller Note. It also states that good-faith set-off is not a default under the Note.
- That right, and any dispute about the underlying indemnity claim, is governed by **New York law** and must be brought exclusively in **New York County** courts (APA §§11.9, 11.10).
- The Seller Note is governed by **Delaware law**, with exclusive jurisdiction in the **Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware** (or the Delaware Superior or federal court as fallback) (Note §12).
- APA §11.12 does **not** resolve this in Prodeth's favor. Although the APA generally prevails over Ancillary Agreements, §11.12 expressly carves out each Ancillary Agreement's "own governing-law and forum clauses." The Note's Delaware clauses therefore stand.
- The Note itself does not mention the set-off right. Its Event of Default in §8(a) is triggered by non-payment after a 5-Business-Day grace period, and §9.1 permits acceleration.

**Why it matters to Prodeth**

- Suppose Prodeth withholds an interest or principal payment under §9.8 (for example, on a pending environmental or NSF claim). Toulous, or a transferee (see Issue 6), could sue on the Note in Delaware, declare an Event of Default and seek acceleration plus the 2% default interest and collection costs.
- Meanwhile, the underlying indemnity dispute and the validity of the set-off must be litigated in New York.
- The result is **parallel proceedings**, a risk of **inconsistent rulings**, and a real risk that the Delaware court enforces the Note as a self-contained instrument without giving effect to the APA set-off. That would turn Prodeth's main source of security (the $6,000,000 Note, which exceeds the $3,150,000 escrow) into a liability.

**Recommended fix**

- Conform Note §12 to New York governing law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the New York County courts, matching APA §§11.9–11.10.
- Add an express set-off clause to the Note itself:
  - all payments are subject to Buyer's rights under APA §9.8;
  - good-faith set-off is not an Event of Default and does not trigger default interest or acceleration; and
  - every transferee takes subject to those rights.
- As a belt-and-braces step, amend APA §11.12 to provide that the APA governs any dispute concerning set-off against the Note.

---

### Issue 5: The 9-month survival period ends before the 12-month NSF recertification audit

**Where:** APA §9.1(a), §6.10 and §4.14; Escrow Agreement §1.2 ("Release Date") and §5.1.

**What the documents say**

- Non-Fundamental representations survive only until **nine (9) months after the Closing Date**, and claims not noticed by then are barred (§9.1(a)).
- That includes the §4.14 representation that each Product holds a valid **NSF/ANSI/CAN 60** certification and conforms to its certified formulation on file. It is not a Fundamental Representation.
- §6.10 schedules the NSF recertification audit of the transferred Products and the Ashby Falls Facility to be completed **within twelve (12) months after the Closing Date**.
- The escrow also releases at nine months (Escrow Agreement Release Date).

**Why it matters to Prodeth**

- The recertification audit is the event most likely to reveal a §4.14 breach, such as formulation drift, unqualified raw-material suppliers or labeling nonconformities.
- On the current timetable, the audit can legitimately finish in months 9–12, after the representation and the escrow have lapsed. Prodeth would then have no claim.
- New York generally enforces contractually shortened claim periods.
- Loss of NSF certification would be serious. It would jeopardize sales for potable-water use and the municipal supply contracts themselves.
- Dr. Fannick's retention bonus (Employment Agreement §4.3) is also keyed to audit completion. This confirms the parties expect the audit to run late in the first year.

**Recommended fix**

- Carve §4.14 (and, ideally, §4.13 and §4.11 to the extent they relate to certification) out of §9.1(a).
- Have §4.14 survive until the later of:
  - 18 months after Closing; and
  - 90 days after the NSF recertification audit is completed and its final report is issued.
- Extend the escrow Release Date to match, or hold back a portion of the escrow until that date.
- Consider making §4.14 a specific indemnity, outside the basket and preferably outside the cap.

---

### Issue 6: The Seller Note is freely transferable, including to a Prodeth competitor

**Where:** Seller Note §10.1, read with §7 (reporting) and §§8–9 (default and acceleration).

**What the documents say**

- Holder may sell, assign, pledge or otherwise transfer the Note, in whole or in part, "**to any Person, without the consent of Maker**" (§10.1). The only obligation is to give notice after the fact (§10.2).
- Every transferee "shall succeed to all of the rights of Holder."
- Those rights include the §7 reporting package:
  - **monthly unaudited consolidated financial statements** of Prodeth;
  - annual audited financials;
  - a **customer-concentration report** naming each customer above 5% of revenue, with the revenue and contract for each; and
  - any other information Holder reasonably requests.

**Why it matters to Prodeth**

- A competitor in water treatment chemicals could buy the Note, possibly at a discount, and receive Prodeth's consolidated financials and municipal customer and contract data every month for three years. That is a serious commercial and antitrust problem. The parties' own Confidentiality Agreement §3.6 treats customer-specific information as "Clean Team Only."
- The transferee would also hold the Note's acceleration remedies, and could use a set-off dispute (Issue 4) as leverage.
- Transfer could also complicate Prodeth's senior-lender subordination arrangements under Note §6.3.

**Recommended fix**

- Amend §10.1 so that any transfer requires Maker's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, with two exceptions:
  - transfers to Toulous's Affiliates or members; and
  - collateral pledges to Toulous's bona fide lenders.
- Absolutely prohibit transfers to any Competitor (define the term by reference to the Restricted Business) and to distressed-debt or activist investors.
- Make any transfer in breach void.
- Require each transferee to:
  - sign a confidentiality undertaking at least as protective as the Confidentiality Agreement;
  - accept the subordination agreement; and
  - take subject to Prodeth's set-off rights.
- Separately, narrow §7:
  - quarterly rather than monthly financials;
  - no customer-level identification (aggregate concentration data only); and
  - all reporting expressly confidential.

---

## 3. Other Observations (lower priority)

- **Escrow sizing versus exposure.** The $3,150,000 escrow is below the $4,200,000 Cap Amount, and it releases at nine months. Once Issues 1 and 5 are fixed, consider a larger or longer escrow. Otherwise rely on the Note set-off, which makes Issues 4 and 6 more important.
- **Note Event of Default §8(f).** A sale of substantially all of the Purchased Assets, other than to an Affiliate that assumes the Note, is an Event of Default. Prodeth should check that this does not restrict ordinary-course financing, sale-leasebacks or a future group reorganization.
- **Joint Press Release (dated September 14, 2026).** It says closing is subject to "receipt of certain third-party consents." That statement does **not** make the Ashcombe consent a closing condition under the APA. The APA conditions are limited to the Required Consents (see Issue 3). No action is needed on the release itself, apart from making sure any post-Closing announcement is cleared under APA §6.7.
- **Confidentiality Agreement (March 9, 2026).** It expires March 9, 2028, except for trade secrets. Its §8 says it continues unless a definitive agreement provides otherwise, and the APA does not supersede it. No issue for Prodeth. Its §6 non-solicit expressly permits the Fannick hire.
- **Fannick Employment Agreement.** It is consistent with the APA and conditional on Closing (§2.1). It is undated and unsigned, and executing it is a closing condition (APA §7.2(f)), so this should be tracked.

---

## 4. Missing or Incomplete Items

The following documents are referenced but **not in the folder**, or are incomplete. Several bear directly on the issues above:

1. **Disclosure Schedule.** It is referenced throughout the APA (§§2.1(c), 2.2, 2.7, 4.9, 4.14, 4.15, 6.6). It also contains key definitions that are not otherwise defined in the APA, including "Encumbrances" and "Permitted Encumbrances." "Material Adverse Effect," "Closing Working Capital" and "Estimated Working Capital Adjustment" are also undefined in the APA as provided. We need to see it, particularly the §4.14 NSF list and the Assigned Contracts list.
2. **Ashcombe Supply Agreement** (and the Brennock and Tillery agreements). We have only the board consent's description of the Ashcombe consent requirement. The actual assignment and change-of-control clauses, termination rights and any pre-Closing performance issues should be reviewed (relevant to Issues 2 and 3).
3. **Ashcombe, Brennock and Tillery consents.** None is in the folder. There is no evidence that any has been requested or obtained.
4. **Phase I Environmental Site Assessment** (Kestrel Ridge, July 22, 2026). It is referenced in the side letter and Annex A but not provided. We should also ask whether a Phase II was done or is needed, given Issue 1.
5. **Toulous member approval.** Board Resolution 6 requires member approval of the sale of substantially all assets under the Operating Agreement. No member consent is in the folder. The Operating Agreement is also not provided.
6. **Prodeth's own board authorization**, the secretary's and officer's certificates, and the deed for the Ashby Falls Facility (APA §3.2(c)) are not in the folder.
7. **Senior Debt documentation and form of subordination agreement** (Note §6). These are needed to confirm the payment-blockage terms and how they interact with set-off.
8. **Payoff letters and lien releases** for Toulous's secured debt (Board Resolution 7). These are needed for title free and clear (APA §4.4).
9. **Execution blanks.**
   - Closing-date documents (Bill of Sale, Note, Escrow Agreement, Side Letter) are undated and unsigned. That is expected for agreed-form documents.
   - The Escrow Agreement Schedule A (authorized representatives) is blank and must be completed for the call-back procedure.
   - The APA signature blocks lack signatory names. We should confirm we hold the fully executed APA.
10. **Board consent timing.** The board approved a September 9 draft, and the APA was signed September 14. Approval of changes is evidenced by execution (Resolution 1), but we should confirm no material changes were made outside the scope of that approval.
11. **Transfer documentation for the State Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (SPDES) and air permits** (Side Letter §4), and the **NSF transfer submission** (APA §6.10). Neither is yet in the file.

---

## 5. Recommended Next Steps

1. Send Toulous's counsel a markup covering:
   - deletion or limitation of Side Letter §2 (Issue 1);
   - revised APA §§2.3(c)/2.4 and deletion of §9.5(d) (Issue 2);
   - addition of the Ashcombe consent to §4.5(a) (Issue 3);
   - extended survival for §4.14 and a matching escrow release (Issue 5); and
   - a revised Note: New York law and forum, an express set-off clause, transfer restrictions and narrowed reporting (Issues 4 and 6).
2. Request the missing items in Section 4, the Ashcombe consent and the Disclosure Schedule as a priority.
3. Advise Prodeth not to sign the Side Letter in its current form.
4. Keep the Outside Date (January 15, 2027) in view. Consider an extension if the Ashcombe consent cannot be obtained in time.

Happy to discuss or turn the markups.

---

## I. Summary

I reviewed all nine documents in the folder:

1. Asset Purchase Agreement dated September 14, 2026 (APA)
2. Fannick Executive Employment Agreement
3. Bill of Sale and Assignment and Assumption Agreement
4. Subordinated Promissory Note (Seller Note)

- Purchase Price is $42,000,000 (APA §2.5).

---

## II. Issues

### Issue 1: Side Letter narrows the environmental cap carve-out (High)

**Where:** Closing Side Letter §2 (and Annex A), read with APA §§1.1, 9.5(b)(iii) and 11.12.

**What it does:**
- Under the APA, "Pre-Closing Environmental Liabilities" covers *all* pre-Closing environmental conditions at the Purchased Assets, including the Ashby Falls Facility. It applies whether the conditions are known or unknown, and whether or not they were disclosed or appear in any report.
- APA §9.5(b)(iii) takes those Losses outside the $4,200,000 Cap Amount, whether claimed under §9.2(a) or §9.2(c).
- Side Letter §2 states that the definition "is hereby amended and restated in its entirety." The new definition covers only Liabilities arising from the "Identified Environmental Conditions." Those are the five recognized environmental conditions from the Kestrel Ridge Phase I Report that are listed in Annex A.
- The Side Letter is expressly entered into under APA §11.8 (Side Letter preamble and §5.1).
- Under APA §11.12, a §11.8 amendment takes precedence over the APA itself.

**Why it matters to Prodeth:**
- The Side Letter is presented as a Seller remediation undertaking. In practice, it removes unidentified contamination from the uncapped carve-out. Examples include undiscovered subsurface releases beneath the blending facility, PFAS, and historic acrylamide or epichlorohydrin leaching outside the Annex A areas.
- Prodeth's recovery for that contamination would then fall back on:
  - the §4.13 environmental representation, which is knowledge-qualified on Releases and survives only 9 months; and
  - the general indemnity, which is capped at $4,200,000.
- The redefinition also flows into §2.4(a) (Excluded Liabilities) and Bill of Sale §3.3. Non-Annex A pre-Closing environmental liabilities are therefore arguably no longer expressly retained by Seller under §2.4(a). They would remain Excluded Liabilities only through the §2.4 catch-all ("all Liabilities of Seller other than the Assumed Liabilities"), and §9.5(a) caps those claims.
- At a chemical blending site with historic drum storage, bulk acid-salt tank farms and an outfall to Mill Race Brook, unknown contamination is the exposure most in need of protection.

**Recommended fix:**
- Strike Side Letter §2 entirely. The remediation covenant in §3 works without it, because §3 can refer directly to the "Identified Environmental Conditions."
- If Seller insists on a defined term for the remediation scope, add a separate defined term (for example, "Remediation Liabilities"). State expressly that the APA definition of Pre-Closing Environmental Liabilities, and its use in §§2.4(a) and 9.5(b)(iii), is unaffected.
- Also consider tightening §3.2. As drafted, it requires only "commercially reasonable efforts" to finish within 24 months. We should seek a firm completion obligation and an escrow or holdback to secure it.

### Issue 2: Prodeth's indemnity for Seller's pre-Closing contract liabilities is uncapped (High)

**Where:** APA §2.3(c), §9.3(b), §9.5(c)–(d) and §9.1(c).

**What it does:**
- §2.3(c) makes "all Liabilities under the Assigned Contracts, whether arising before or after the Closing" Assumed Liabilities.
- §9.3(b) requires Prodeth to indemnify Seller for any Assumed Liability.
- §9.5(c) caps Prodeth's indemnity at the Cap Amount, but §9.5(d) then provides that "no limitation in this Section 9.5" applies to §9.3(b).
- §9.1(c) allows §9.3(b) claims "at any time."

**Why it matters to Prodeth:**
- Prodeth takes on, without any cap or time limit, Seller's own pre-Closing breaches of the municipal supply contracts. These include off-spec or non-conforming deliveries, late-delivery penalties and liquidated damages, and product-quality claims from utilities.
- In potable-water supply, a single off-spec coagulant lot can lead to treatment failures, regulatory penalties and third-party claims.
- §2.3(c) also cuts against Seller's §4.5(b) representation that there is no material breach of any Assigned Contract. If Seller breached before Closing, the liability is "assumed" by Prodeth. Prodeth would have to indemnify Seller for that liability while also trying to recover against Seller for the same breach under a capped, 9-month representation claim.

**Recommended fix:**
- Revise §2.3(c) to cover only Liabilities under the Assigned Contracts "to the extent arising from and relating to performance required after the Closing, and not arising from any breach or default by Seller on or before the Closing."
- Add a corresponding Excluded Liability in §2.4 for pre-Closing breaches and for products shipped before Closing.
- Delete §9.5(d), or at least limit it to post-Closing obligations, so that §9.3(b) is subject to the Cap Amount.

### Issue 3: The Ashcombe consent is neither a Required Consent nor a closing condition (High)

**Where:** APA §§2.1(c), 4.5(a), 6.3, 7.2(c) and 3.2(d); Toulous Board Consent, Recital 1.5 and Resolution 3.

**What it does:**
- The Ashcombe Supply Agreement is an Assigned Contract (APA §2.1(c)).
- The "Required Consents" in §4.5(a) cover only the Brennock Regional Water Commission and the Tillery Municipal Utilities District.
- Toulous's own Board Consent (Recital 1.5) states two relevant facts:
  - the Ashcombe Supply Agreement accounted for approximately 31% of the Business's 2025 revenue; and
  - the agreement may not be assigned, nor may Toulous effect "any sale of all or substantially all of the assets used in its performance," without the "prior written consent of the Authority."
- Resolution 3 only authorizes officers to *seek* that consent.
- §6.3 (efforts to obtain consents), §3.2(d) (closing deliverables) and §7.2(c) (Buyer's closing condition) all refer only to the Required Consents.
- Nothing in the folder shows that the Authority has consented.

**Why it matters to Prodeth:**
- As drafted, the Ashcombe consent is not a condition to Prodeth's obligation to close.
- If the Authority refuses consent, stays silent, or treats the sale as a breach and terminates, Prodeth could still be required to close and pay the full $42,000,000. It would do so without the Business's largest customer contract.
- Prodeth's fallback would be weak. §4.5(a) is inaccurate on its face, but a claim for that inaccuracy would be:
  - subject to the $210,000 basket and the $4,200,000 cap;
  - limited by the 9-month survival period; and
  - an uncertain way of measuring loss from a lost contract.
- The §7.2(e) MAE condition is undefined in the APA (see Part III) and is a weak substitute.
- The Press Release and its forward-looking statements say closing is subject to "receipt of certain third-party consents." Readers could assume Ashcombe is among them, but under the APA as drafted it is not.

**Recommended fix:**
- Amend §4.5(a) to add the Ashcombe County Water Authority's consent as a Required Consent. The definition should cover both the assignment and the sale of substantially all assets used in performance.
- Make that consent an express condition in §7.2(c). It should be in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Prodeth and unconditional, with no adverse amendment to pricing or term.
- Extend the §6.3 efforts covenant and the §6.4 notice covenant to the Ashcombe consent.
- If Seller resists, at minimum include:
  - a specific, uncapped indemnity or purchase price adjustment tied to loss of the Ashcombe contract; and
  - a Prodeth walk right if the consent is not obtained by the Outside Date.
- Ask Seller for the status of its approach to the Authority now.

### Issue 4: The 9-month survival period ends before the NSF recertification audit (Medium–High)

**Where:** APA §9.1(a), §4.14 and §6.10; Escrow Agreement §1.2 (Release Date) and §5.1.

**What it does:**
- Non-Fundamental representations, including the §4.14 NSF/ANSI/CAN 60 certification representation, survive only "until nine (9) months after the Closing Date." Claims not noticed by then are barred.
- §6.10 requires Prodeth to complete the recertification audit of the transferred Products and the Ashby Falls Facility "within twelve (12) months after the Closing Date."
- The escrow Release Date also falls at nine months.

**Why it matters to Prodeth:**
- The recertification audit is the event most likely to reveal a §4.14 breach, such as a nonconformity between blended products and their formulations on file, an uncertified raw-material supplier, or a labeling defect.
- The audit can lawfully finish after the representation has expired. New York generally enforces contractually shortened claim periods, so Prodeth could be left without a claim.
- The escrow will also have been released to Seller by then.
- Loss of NSF certification would stop sales into potable-water applications, which is the core of the Business.
- Fannick's retention bonus is also tied to completion of this audit (Fannick Agreement §4.3). The audit timing is therefore commercially significant.

**Recommended fix:**
- Extend survival of §4.14 (and ideally §§4.11 and 4.13) to the later of (a) 18 months after Closing and (b) 90 days after completion of the §6.10 audit.
- Alternatively, add a specific indemnity for NSF certification nonconformities that is not subject to §9.1(a).
- Conform the escrow Release Date, or hold back an NSF-specific portion of the escrow until the audit is completed.

### Issue 5: The Seller Note is freely transferable, including to a competitor (Medium)

**Where:** Seller Note §10.1, read with §7 and §§8(b)/9.1.

**What it does:**
- §10.1 allows the Holder to "sell, assign, pledge or otherwise transfer this Note, in whole or in part... to any Person, without the consent of Maker." A transferee "shall succeed to all of the rights of Holder."
- §7 requires Prodeth to deliver the following to the Holder:
  - monthly unaudited consolidated financial statements;
  - annual audited financial statements;
  - a customer-concentration report naming each customer above 5% of revenue, with the revenue attributable to that customer and the governing contract; and
  - any other information the Holder reasonably requests.

**Why it matters to Prodeth:**
- Toulous could sell the Note, including at a discount, to a competitor in the municipal water treatment chemicals market, or partial interests could end up with competitors.
- That competitor would then receive, for up to 36 months, Prodeth's consolidated financial information and a list of its key municipal customers with revenue and contract detail. This is precisely the information that drives municipal bidding.
- The Note contains no confidentiality obligation on the Holder.
- Failure to deliver the §7 reports is an Event of Default (§8(b)) with acceleration rights (§9.1). A hostile Holder would therefore have leverage over Prodeth.
- Sharing this information could also raise antitrust information-exchange concerns, which the parties themselves acknowledged in Confidentiality Agreement §3.6.
- The restriction in §10.3 on Prodeth's own assignment shows the imbalance.

**Recommended fix:** Revise §10.1 to:
- require Prodeth's prior written consent to any transfer, not to be unreasonably withheld, except for transfers to Toulous's Affiliates or members;
- flatly prohibit transfers to any Competitor (to be defined by reference to the Restricted Business) or to any Affiliate of a Competitor;
- add a confidentiality covenant binding the Holder and each transferee as to §7 information;
- narrow §7 to quarterly summary financials, delete or anonymize the customer-concentration report, and limit §7(d); and
- make any transfer in breach void.
